body: Hmm, how long ago did you pull from master? I _just_ did a release using master and the tests passed fine during that.
Oh I see, you're using Node.js master. Shouldn't you file an issue with Node.js for this problem?

I am one of the collaborators on the node project. This was discovered during smoke testing. I wanted to let ya'll know that you are broken on master as we will be cutting v6 in the next month. Some of the major changes on master are breaking. I'm doing some forensics to figure out exactly what it is.

I'm not 100% if this is a regression in node yet, or a change will need to be made in eslint due to Semver Major changes.

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body:
In the current versions of node path.\* can be called on any arbitrary
value and will return an empty string on invalid input.

As of node v6 path will assert that values passed to it are strings,
and as such will throw on `undefined`

This commit moved the logic of using `path.extname` inside of the
processText  function in `lib/cli-engine.js`. so that it will not call
`path.extname` if a filename is not passed.

This change should not affect any other parts of the system, and the
test suite is 100% working on node v4, v5, and master.

fixes #5678
